extractedItems.title: Who decides if a ball is unplayable?
extractedItems.question: If your ball ends up in a really bad spot, like under a tree, who gets to decide whether it’s unplayable?

choices.text: The player
The marker
Your opponent
A referee

extractedItems.explanation: The player is always free to decide if their ball is unplayable. You don’t need agreement from anyone else.
extractedItems.imagePrompt: A teenage golfer stands next to a ball that is stuck under tree roots, looking puzzled and thinking about what to do.
extractedItems.imageAlt: A teen golfer next to a ball under tree roots, appearing unsure.

extractedItems.title: What are your options for an unplayable ball?
extractedItems.question: If you declare your ball unplayable, which of the following actions can you take for a penalty of one stroke? (Select all that apply)

choices.text: Drop the ball within two club-lengths of where it lies
Go back as far as you like on the line from your ball to the hole and drop there
Replay the shot from where you last played
Drop the ball on the green for free
Ask your friend what to do

extractedItems.explanation: You can drop within two club-lengths, back on the line, or replay the last shot, all for one penalty stroke.
extractedItems.imagePrompt: A teenage boy golfer with a ball under a bush, thinking about three different drop options: two club-lengths, back on a line, or to replay from the previous spot.
extractedItems.imageAlt: Teen golfer has a ball under a bush and is imagining three choices for dropping.

extractedItems.title: What happens if your dropped ball rolls back to the bad spot?
extractedItems.question: You drop your ball after declaring it unplayable, but it rolls back to the same impossible position. What are your options?

choices.text: You must play the ball as it now lies, or declare it unplayable again
You can drop again for free
You get to move the ball to a better spot without penalty
You must give up the hole

extractedItems.explanation: You either have to play the ball as it lies or you can declare it unplayable again, taking another penalty.
extractedItems.imagePrompt: A teen golfer watches as their dropped ball rolls right back under the same tree roots, looking frustrated.
extractedItems.imageAlt: Teen golfer drops a ball and it returns to an awkward spot under tree roots.

choices.text: The player
The marker
Your opponent
A referee

reviewedItems.explanation: Only the player can decide if their ball is unplayable, no one else can make this decision for them.

reviewedItems.title: What are your options for an unplayable ball?
reviewedItems.question: If you declare your ball unplayable, which of the following actions are allowed for a one-stroke penalty? (Select all that apply)

choices.text: Drop the ball within two club-lengths of where it lies
Go back as far as you like in line with the hole and drop there
Replay the shot from where you last played
Drop the ball on the green without penalty
Ask your friend to choose for you

reviewedItems.explanation: You may drop within two club-lengths, go back on a straight line keeping the spot between you and the hole, or replay the last shot, all for one penalty stroke.

reviewedItems.title: What if your dropped ball ends up back in the same spot?
reviewedItems.question: You drop your ball for relief but it rolls back to the same tough place as before. What can you do next?

choices.text: Play the ball as it is, or declare it unplayable again
Drop again for free
Move the ball to an easier spot without penalty
Pick up the ball and stop playing the hole

reviewedItems.explanation: You must play the ball as it lies, or you may declare it unplayable again and take another penalty stroke.
